objective_for_doctor: Perform a skin examination and diagnose the skin condition presented by the patient.
chief_complaint: Brown, greasy-looking lesions on the forehead

fragments.text: The patient presents for a routine visit and has no complaints other than the recent appearance of several brown, greasy-looking lesions on his forehead. He mentions that these lesions have developed over the past few months and are bothersome because he cannot seem to remove them despite attempting to peel them off.
Non-removable despite attempts to peel off
No significant past medical history. No history of skin cancer or extensive sun exposure. No recent changes in medications or topical treatments.
Retired postal worker, non-smoker, and drinks alcohol socially. Enjoys gardening but always wears a hat for sun protection.
Denies itchiness, pain, bleeding from the lesions, fever, weight loss, or any other systemic symptoms.

exam_leaves.text: Multiple well-defined, brown, greasy plaques of varying sizes noted on the forehead. No erythema or edema around the lesions.
Lesions are slightly raised above the skin surface and have a rough texture. No tenderness on palpation.
A network of cerebriform patterns without evidence of melanocytic activity.

test_leaves.text: Hyperkeratosis with horn cysts, consistent with seborrheic keratosis.
